lines: Four slow envelopes that switch themselves on and off: a shared timer marks out the gaps, each lane rolls its own chance of firing at one, and each fades up and down over seconds to drive a VCA
Varies the length of each gap at random, by nothing at the counter-clockwise end and by up to 30% either way at the clockwise end
Sets how long the gaps between events last, 90 seconds at the counter-clockwise end and 5 seconds at the clockwise end on a logarithmic scale; a cable in the Density CV input takes it out of use
Varies how long each event runs at random, by nothing at the counter-clockwise end and by up to half either way at the clockwise end
On starts the enabled lane with the highest Weight whenever no lane is running, so the module never falls silent; its lamp is white while this is on and red while it is off
Each press switches that lane on or off; a lane switched off holds its output at 0V whatever its Floor knob says, and its lamp turns red
Sets the chance that this lane fires when a gap ends, from never at the counter-clockwise end to every time at the clockwise end
Sets how long this lane stays on once it fires, 5 seconds at the counter-clockwise end and 90 seconds at the clockwise end on a logarithmic scale, and its fade times are taken from it too
Sets the level this lane rests at between events, 0V at the counter-clockwise end and the full 5V at the clockwise end, with the envelope rising from there
Sets the gap length outright, 0V giving 90 seconds and 10V giving 5 seconds; while a cable is here the Density knob is left out of the reckoning
A rising edge past 1V switches that lane on for a full duration with its jitter, even while it is already running; the lane's enable button has to be on for this to reach it
That lane's envelope, 0V to 5V, rising and falling on one-pole curves whose times come from its Duration knob and resting at the level its Floor knob sets
Note — this module works on a scale of seconds to minutes: gaps of 5 to 90 seconds, events of 5 to 90 seconds and fades measured in seconds, so a patch takes a while to show what it does
Note — a lane's attack is a fifth of its Duration setting held between 30ms and 2 seconds, and its release is two fifths of it held between 300ms and 25 seconds
Note — a lane's lamp is red while that lane is switched off and white while it is on, its brightness following the envelope that lane is putting out
Note — the four enable buttons are saved with the patch, and nothing else about the module's state is, so the gaps and the events start afresh each time it is loaded

phrasing.notes: Read at commit 811b78f, the repository head. Six commits carry the installed 2.2.0. The installed res/Phrasing.png matches the blob first written at 218dfb2, which narrows it to 218dfb2 or 811b78f, and those two differ only in the density CV: 218dfb2 writes the scaled voltage into the Density parameter with setValue, 811b78f keeps it in a local. The disassembly of Phrasing::process settles it - at 0x5fdc the params pointer is loaded, the input voltage is scaled by 0.1 and clamped into a register, and nothing is stored back into the parameter - so 811b78f shipped and the Density knob does not move when CV is patched. Earlier 2.2.0 commits also used single green lane lamps where the installed binary instantiates MediumLight<RedGreenBlueLight>, which agrees. The README says the trig inputs need about 1.7V; the code uses dsp::SchmittTrigger at its defaults, so the threshold is 1V, and the lines say 1V. The README describes the Density CV as a knob-plus-CV control; the code replaces the knob outright while a cable is patched. A lane switched off with its enable button outputs 0V and ignores its Floor knob, which the README does not say. With Guarantee one on and every enabled lane's Weight at zero, the first enabled lane is chosen rather than the highest-weight one; that case is left out of the switch's line. The Gap Jitter and Dur Jitter knobs are scaled by 0.30 and 0.50 before use, so their full travel is plus or minus 30% and plus or minus half. The panel prints no name on the Guarantee switch, the Density CV jack, the four enable buttons or the four lamps. The maker's own panel and plugin.json call the four channels lanes, and the lines follow that. Nothing is polyphonic: every jack is read with getVoltage() and no channel, and the binary imports neither setChannels nor getPolyVoltage.
